exactToolArguments.prompt:
Draw NEW ORIGINAL ASHVEIL actual airborne FLIGHT animation. Use the attached OWN crow idle and feeding originals ONLY for the SAME individual bird identity, head/body proportions, chunky short charcoal beak, small dark eyes, rounded compact skull, layered blue-black feather texture and short fan tail. DO NOT copy the standing/feeding posture. This is one small crow, NOT an eagle, owl, bat, raven-headed humanoid or different model. No markings/courier gear. Rich muted textured pixel-style rendering with restrained cool-grey feathers, consistent fixed slightly elevated game camera.

Exactly FOUR ROWS x FOUR COLUMNS = SIXTEEN newly drawn distinct isolated FULL-BODY flight poses. Row1 flies DOWN toward viewer, row2 flies LEFT, row3 flies RIGHT, row4 flies UP away from viewer. Every pose keeps that row's heading, beak axis and tail opposite head. Never turn a rear bird sideways to expose an eye. Front/rear both wings are actual left/right anatomical wings; side views show the nearer wing clearly and the far wing in the proper partly occluded offset. Exactly TWO wings, never extra fan-shaped arms or duplicate wings.

Each row is a continuous wingbeat LOOP with the SAME stable airborne breast/body centre and SAME head and skull size in all4columns. The body is in a naturally forward-leaning/streamlined flight attitude, visibly suspended, NOT a standing upright crow with flapping arms. Fold BOTH skinny feet and toes up against the lower belly/rear body throughout, with no leg stretched toward imaginary ground, no stance, no planted claws. Feet may be partly hidden but must never become a third/fourth leg. The head stays aligned forward and the SAME beak/head/tail proportions are maintained as the wings rotate.

COLUMN1 UPSTROKE APEX: both long feathered wings lifted high ABOVE the back, elbows slightly bent, finger-feathers fan outward, broad open V; tucked feet. COLUMN2 POWER STROKE MIDPOINT: the TWO wings extend broadly SIDEWAYS roughly at the breast/body horizontal plane, longest clear broad span, primary feather fans articulated, head/body hold stable and forward. COLUMN3 DOWNSTROKE BOTTOM: BOTH wings push DOWN BELOW the breast and toward its sides, clearly lower than body centre, feather tips point down/out in a strong downstroke, still feet tucked; do not substitute folded idle wings. COLUMN4 RECOVERY RETURN: both elbows flex and wrists draw wings partway UP toward the back, narrower bent-wing silhouette between bottom and top, distinct from columns1/2/3. Wings are recovering toward column1. All4phases must show a real change in vertical wing position and feather silhouette; no repeated idle or motionless glide. For rear row show back/shoulders/tail, head atop/in front of back; visible face is not required. For side rows retain whole far wing logically attached, not two stacked near wings.

Keep body centre/head stationary within a row while wing tips move, slight natural breast bob only. Frame widths may change but each skull has identical size; DO NOT zoom/enlarge individual phases. At game scale the skull/body must match the original compact crow, while open wings naturally span beyond its folded body. No gigantic head, needle beak, furry mammal feet, clipped wing tips or isolated feather fragments.

CRITICAL ATLAS SAFETY: make the canvas square and give all16flight birds exceptionally wide truly transparent alpha-zero gaps on EVERY side. Every COMPLETE widest wingspan/tallest raised-wing silhouette occupies at most60%of its cell width and60%of its height. Leave enough empty transparent margin between rows for up and down strokes; no wingtip overlaps neighbouring cells. Full left/right wing feathers, beak, both tucked feet and tail included, closed complete forms. NO borders/text/grid/checkerboard, NO floor/soil/objects/carcass/food/blood/shadow, no glow/spotlight/clouds, no Z/altitude/UI/balloon or motion trails. Only the sixteen actual airborne crow bodies on transparent PNG. Draw original pixels; no commercial-game copying.
